data.long_meaning: Eswar is a name derived from Sanskrit, meaning 'Lord of the Universe'. In Hindu mythology, Lord Shiva is often referred to as Eswar, representing the supreme power and creator of the universe. The name Eswar carries the meaning “Lord of the Universe” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Eswar usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of the universe and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.cultural_impact: The name Eswar holds great significance in Indian culture, particularly in Hinduism, where Lord Shiva is a primary deity. It is widely used as a title or name for temples and idols dedicated to Lord Shiva. Devotional hymns, songs, and literature often use this name when referring to the deity. In various rituals and ceremonies, it is common to chant the name 'Eswar' as a form of worship and invocation.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hinduism, Lord Eswar or Lord Shiva represents the ultimate reality and the supreme power of creation, destruction, and preservation. He is the embodiment of all divine qualities, including love, compassion, purity, and wisdom. Worshipping Lord Eswar is believed to bring spiritual growth, fulfillment, and ultimate liberation from the cycle of birth and death. The name Eswar itself evokes a deep sense of reverence and awe, reminding us of the divine presence that pervades the universe.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Eswar, meaning "Lord of the Universe," symbolizes the divine power and creator of the cosmos in Hinduism. It is a name revered for the supreme god Shiva, representing the absolute consciousness and infinite potentiality.
